### 1.2 BIOS & UEFI

### **Goal**: Screen record the UEFI on your laptops and prepare them for installing an Operating System (OS).

### **Required Materials**:

* HDMI Capture card  
* HDMI cable  
* Obsidian

### Vocabulary

| HDMI Capture Card | Makes the output of your Dell desktop appear as a camera input on your laptop.  | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/captureCard.png" width="300px"> |
| :---- | :---- | ----- |
| **Screenshot** | A photo of your desktop. It’s called the 'snipping' tool. | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/snipToolwin.png" width="800px"> |
| **Firmware** | The software that controls the motherboard. | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/dell_POST_screen.png" width="800px"> |
| **BIOS  (Basic Input Output System)** | An older firmware style that is largely obsolete. It’s prominent on computers prior to 2008\. This is sometimes called a **Legacy boot**. | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/Dell_BIOS.png" width="800px"> |
| **UEFI  (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface)** | The firmware on computers from 2008 onward. </br> - The mouse works <br/> - Significantly more secure </br> - Allows an OS like Windows to better control the hardware. | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/ASUS_UEFI.png" width="800px"> |
| **Secure Boot** | A feature of UEFI firmware that refuses any operating system key signature that’s not hard baked into the firmware. Typically allowed: Windows Ubuntu RHEL Fedora ESXi Every other OS is blocked from booting. | <img src="https://github.com/CRyan-EPIC/Classes/blob/main/ComputerTechnicianA+/unit_1/img/Secure_Boot_Violation.png" width="800px"> |

**Part I** \- [Watch Me](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LGz0Io_dh_I) (5:36)

**Part II** \- Obsidian Tutorial

* **Choose X of the following, where X is the number of members in your group.** If you are solo, you choose one tutorial. If you are in groups of two, you need two different tutorials. Groups of three need three different tutorials.  
* Create a **2-3 page tutorial** on Obsidian with at least 5 screenshots explaining how to complete the following:

| 🟢 | How to enable/disable secure boot and change the boot order (recommended). Changing the CMOS battery and changing the clock How to get into the BIOS and reset the firmware back to defaults. How to limit your personal laptops battery charge limit to 80%. |
| :---- | :---- |
| 🟦 | How to update the firmware safely (ask me about this before proceeding). |
| ⯁ | Short tutorial on using the UEFI shell. How to import a MOK.  |
| ⯁⯁ | Safely underclocking your personal laptop to save battery life. I do not recommend you overclock your equipment. |

**How to receive credit:**

* Your tutorial contains clear and articulate complete sentences with at least 5 properly formatting UEFI screenshots.  
* Answer the following questions at the end of your tutorial:  
  * What does POST mean?  
  * What is the CMOS battery for?  
  * What’s the difference between UEFI and BIOS?  
  * What did you learn?
